newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benpres move on ABS-CBN positive - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Benpres move on ABS-CBN positive - analysts.

text.p: Plans by Benpres Holdings Corp to transfer its stake in ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp to parent Lopez Inc will hit earnings in the short-term but in the longer run will be positive, analysts said on Monday.

The proposal, to be put to shareholders later this month, would divest Benpres of its media assets and so allow foreigners to buy shares in the firm which has taken an increasing role in a variety of infrastructure projects.
The Philippines bars foreigners from directly investing in local media
"It will be a short-term loss but medium to long-term gain," said Conrad Andres, research head of DBP-Daiwa Securities, since ABS-CBN contributes 50 percent of Benpres' net income.

"It needs to raise its profile among the investor community especially among foreigners. There has been a change in orientation from a simple investment holding company to an infrastructure firm. It will be easier to access the global capital markets," he added.
Benpres announced earlier that it would transfer its 71-percent stake in ABS-CBN and 20 percent in SkyVision Corp to Lopez Inc. Lopez Inc owns 82.5 percent of Benpres.

"There's a notional earnings per share (impact)," said Jose Salceda, director of SBC Warburg, noting that under the proposal Benpres has the option to buy back shares of the media companies at the same price at which they were transferred to Lopez.
Benpres estimates its 1996 net income was 1.82 billion pesos, up from 1.62 billion in 1995.
Analysts said foreign participation in Benpres would allow it to easily raise capital in international markets to help fund its projects such as toll roads, telecommunications and property.
ING Barings analyst Giovanni de la Rosa said Benpres needed to allow foreign investors to buy its shares ahead of a planned rights offer this year to raise 8.5 to 9.5 billion pesos.
ABS-CBN is the country's most profitable television network, while SkyVision is a cable television company.

"The transaction is a pass-on. It shouldn't impact on earnings. The idea is to capture the economic benefits of the media companies at Benpres," Rafael Andrada, the firm's chief finance officer, told Reuters.

Benpres, whose option to buy back will remain open until Philippine law changes to allow foreigners to buy media shares, will issue proforma earnings reports to include ABS-CBN and SkyVision, he added.
Foreigners currently may only invest in Benpres through Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) listed in Luxembourg.
"Global Depository Receipts, which foreigners now buy in lieu of regular common stock, can now be converted into common shares once the proposal is approved," Benpres said in a statement.
